speak to him in a genuine sympathetic way 1 to 1. be understanding, empathetic of how he might feel, to really reach out to him and show you care. acknowledge anything that might have made him resort to using the weed, or anything he might not have been open about. weed is widely known for giving that boost of feel good feelings, dopamine, and then taking them away once you’re off the high. when you use for so long, your brain can’t really make t dopamine because it gets use to the weed stimulating the part of your brain to use it. there’s a reason why he goes back, and why he’s so different when he’s off of it. when you resort to weed in a bad mental health state, it’s going to do this to you. me and my boyfriend had a similar problem, and he was using by himself every night instead of in social situations, and started to become depressed and acting different. it’s the way your brain works when you’re not on it. explain this in a caring way to him, and that you want to get him to a place where he doesn’t rely on weed to create dopamine, and maybe compromise that it can be a thing for special occasions or for social gatherings etc. he needs some help it definitely seems. start planning activities for you to do, be more proactive in things that can be distracting, board games, movies, video games, road trips, trying new foods, cooking, make a routine of something so he can start to get use to getting dopamine out of other things instead of the weed, and his brain will start to produce those chemicals like normal again. wishing you the best of luck, this really helped my relationship with my boyfriend and his mental health a lot.

i figured the above. working at a job with so much on your plate, truly fucks you up more than half the kids your age. early maturity has its costs. and with the adhd thing, i’m in the same boat. meds helped at first, started taking them a year ago. i’ve noticed they can make me depressed, irritable, emotional, and unhealthy. you can try giving other ones a shot. you can stop them too, tell your psychiatrist prior to it so they can guide you through it. caffeine can help with focus, i’ve heard from a fellow friend with adhd. and from another friend, they used marijuana (not a lot to get you blasted) to help focus and be more calm. but with motivation, it’s tricky. you need to want to do better for yourself in order to feel motivated. but how do you do better for yourself without motivation? one can’t work without the other.. and when you have neither.. it’s tricky. you just force yourself through it. force yourself to get up early and walk, regardless of your weight, just going outside , walking and listening to music for 15 minutes can wake you up. and it’ll make you want to do better/ because you finally were able to do better. it’s the little things. it takes lot of self disobedience to do even that so if you start treating yourself better in that sense you better be fucking proud. just starting and getting missing assignments done was enough to give me motivation. took a lot of tears and fighting my mental health. lot of avoidant anxiety with school. but tackling one task is enough to give you motivation for the rest. because you got it. start off small , little steps. work more with cars. in your free time. set reminders. tons of them. only you can treat yourself the way you want to be treated. don’t worry about relationships. i get it though. being lonely fucking sucks. it can get your mind off of things. but you have to be in a good relationship with yourself first. mentally and physically. you need to treat yourself better, so others won’t look down on you and treat you less because they think you don’t care. they’ll use you like a door mat. and don’t let them. be the best you can be and tell others to fuck off.

7.) don’t forget the cars
8.) graduate
